en.title: Ways to Replace All Question Marks with No Adjacent Repeats
en.description:
The string consists of lowercase letters and question marks; each question mark may be replaced with any lowercase letter, and fixed letters cannot be changed. Find the number of replacements after which no two adjacent characters are equal, modulo 1000000007.

The ranges added by this site for missing bounds and the recovery of source typos are described in the input protocol.
en.input: One line containing s. Full original bounds: 1≤|s|≤100000, and the characters are only a..z or ?.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 650; 25; 0. They have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Use 26 states to record the last letter. For a letter c usable at the current position, the new count equals the prefix's total count minus the count ending in c.
